API Reference

Calculations

class gwsus.calculations.Suspension(name)[source]

Bases: object

calculate_Ek()[source]

Calculates the total kinetic energy.

Collects and adds algebraic kinetic energy terms for all bodies, assigning the result to self.Ek.

Returns:

self.Ek – Algebraic expression of the total kinetic energy.

Return type:

type

Notes

Typically for internal use, but can be called by user.

calculate_Ep()[source]

Calculates the addition of gravitational and axial elastic potential energies.

Adds algebraic expressions of the gravitational and axial elastic potential energies of all bodies and links, assigning the result to self.Ep. The rotational potential energies of links is not calculated here because it requires knowledge of the equilibrium positions of their ends.

Returns:

self.Ep – Algebraic expression of the total potential energy.

Return type:

type

Notes

Typically for internal use, but can be called by user.

calculate_equilibrium_positions(chop=1e-10)[source]
calculate_grav_Ep()[source]

Calculates the total gravitational potential energy.

Collects algebraic gravitational potential energy terms for all bodies, assigning the total sum to self.grav_Ep.

Returns:

self.grav_Ep – Algebraic expression of the total gravitational potential energy.

Return type:

type

Notes

Typically for internal use, but can be called by user.

calculate_link_axial_Ep()[source]

Calculates the total wire elastic axial potential energy.

Collects and adds algebraic wire axial elastic potential energy terms for all wires, assigning the total sum to `self.link_axial_Ep.

Returns:

self.link_axial_Ep – Algebraic expression of the total gravitational potential energy.

Return type:

type

Notes

Typically for internal use, but can be called by user.

calculate_link_torsion_Ep()[source]

Calculates the total link elastic torsional potential energy.

Collects and adds algebraic torsional elastic potential energy terms for all links, assigning the total sum to self.link_torsion_Ep.

Returns:

self.link_torsion_Ep – Algebraic expression of the total gravitational potential energy.

Return type:

type

connect(body_upper, name_point_upper, body_lower, name_point_lower, link)[source]

Establishes a connection between attachment points via a link.

Parameters:

  • body_upper (gwsus.RigidBody) – Body connected to the upper end of the link.

  • name_point_upper (str) – Name of the attachment point set in the upper body.

  • body_lower (gwsus.RigidBody) – Body connected to the lower end of the link.

  • name_point_lower (str) – Name of the attachment point set in the lower body.

  • link (gwsus.Spring or gwsus.Wire) – Link used for connecting the attachment points.

attachment_points_p

A dictionary containing the displacement vectors of the attachment points written in body coordinates w.r.t. the body’s center of mass. * Each key is the name (str) of the attachment point set (e.g., “for_IM”, “for_MIR”). * Each value is a list of column vectors defined as $3 imes 1$ Symengine’s MutableDenseMatrix matrices with numeric entries. * For internal use, but accesible for user’s inspection.

Type:

dict

attachment_points_r

A dictionary containing the displacement vectors of the attachment points written in world coordinates w.r.t. the origin of the world reference frame. * Each key is the name (str) of the attachment point set (e.g., “for_IM”, “for_MIR”). * Each value is a list of column vectors defined as $3 imes 1$ Symengine’s MutableDenseMatrix matrices with symbolic entries. * For internal use, but accesible for user’s inspection.

Type:

dict

calculate_geometry()[source]

Calculates the vector differences between attachment points and their norms.

These quantities are required to calculate the axial and torsional potential energies, and for the animation of the wires.

Notes

Can be called after suspension.connect, and therefore, it’s called in suspension.update via link.update.

gwsus.utils.pendulum_toolkit(sus, path, file_name)[source]

Generates a file with the definition of the model for use in Pendulum Toolkit.

Parameters:

  • sus (gwsus.suspension) – Suspension whose specifications will be written in the file.

  • path (string) – Path to the directory where the file will be saved, e.g., ‘my/mathematica/directory/’.

  • file_name (string) – By convention, the name of the file will be file_name + ‘Defn.m’, e.g., ‘myModelDefn.m’.

Rotation matrix for a … , passive rotation transforming from space to body coordinates in this order: yaw –> pitch –> roll.

  • pitch (various types) – Rotation angle around the transverse axis, measured in radians.
